description: This topic is based on the visual and logical analysis of three-dimensional figures. In competitive exams, questions related to finding the opposite faces of dice and the cutting of painted cubes are primarily asked.

sections.title: Types of Dice
sections.description: Dice are classified into two main types based on the sum of the numbers present on their visible faces.

results: The sum of any two adjacent faces is never 7.
The sum of opposite faces is always exactly 7 (e.g., 1 is opposite 6, 2 is opposite 5, and 3 is opposite 4).
The sum of any two adjacent faces can be exactly 7.
It is not possible to accurately determine the opposite faces from just a single position; multiple positions are required for deduction.

sections.title: Rules to Find Opposite Faces
sections.description: When two or more positions of the exact same dice are given, standard logical rules are applied to deduce the opposite numbers.

results: If only one number is common between the two given positions, start from that common number and write the numbers of both dice in a clockwise direction.
The numbers that align vertically one below the other in this arrangement are opposite faces to each other.
If any two numbers are common between the two given positions, cancel or ignore them.
The remaining third numbers on both dice are always opposite to each other.

sections.title: Open Dice (Unfolded Cube)
sections.description: When a 3D cube is unfolded and laid flat on a 2D plane, its 6 faces become visible. Standard rules apply to find opposite faces when folding it back.

key_concepts.explanation: In the structural figure of an open dice, every alternate face (skipping one face) located in a straight horizontal or vertical line is always opposite to each other.
In an open dice layout, the faces located at the extreme ends (corners) of a shape forming a 'Z' or 'N' are opposite to each other.

sections.title: Cutting of a Painted Cube
sections.description: Mathematical formulas used to determine the count of various types of smaller cubes when a larger uniformly painted cube is cut into smaller identical pieces.

key_concepts.explanation: Here 'n' represents the ratio of the side length of the larger cube to the side length of the smaller cube. (n = Length of larger cube / length of smaller cube)
